title: Intel Offers Innovative Approach to IoT Scaling and Security
summary: Intel announced its Secure Device Onboard (Intel SDO) technology to address the challenges of scaling and securing IoT deployments. Intel SDO automates device onboarding, reducing setup time from hours to seconds and utilizing Intel Enhanced Privacy ID (Intel EPID) for anonymous authentication and secure communication. The technology is being adopted by other silicon providers and integrated into cloud platforms, with early successful implementation by Weatherford in the oil and gas sector.

title: No need to take off your robe. Target will bring the paper towels to you
summary: Target is rolling out a new "drive up" service, currently in trial around Minneapolis and St. Paul, allowing shoppers to order items via an app and have employees bring purchases directly to their cars. This initiative aims to blend the convenience of online shopping with the immediate availability of in-store pickups, competing with similar services offered by retailers like Walmart. The service is being tested for a wider rollout to make shopping quicker and easier for busy customers.

title: How Much Traffic Whole Foods Is Taking From Walmart
summary: Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods and subsequent price cuts led to a significant increase in foot traffic, with a notable portion of new customers coming from Walmart. Research by Thasos Group indicates that 24% of new Whole Foods customers were previously loyal Walmart shoppers. The article also notes the impact on other grocers like Trader Joe's and Sprouts, and speculates on how further price cuts could attract lower-income customers.

title: Amazon said to face EU order to pay millions in back taxes to Luxembourg
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is expected to face an order from the European Union to pay millions of euros in back taxes to Luxembourg, becoming the latest US giant targeted by the bloc's state-aid rules. This decision follows similar actions against Apple and is part of EU Competition Commissioner Margrethe Vestager's crackdown on tax loopholes, aiming to ensure fair competition. The EU has been investigating various individual tax deals and broader tax avoidance schemes across member states since 2013.

title: The New Azrieli Sarona Tower is Israel’s Hottest Tech Real-Estate
summary: The Azrieli Sarona Tower in Tel Aviv is attracting top tech companies like Amazon, Facebook, and Magic Leap, even before its official opening in 2018. Standing at over 830 feet, it is Israel's tallest and widest office building, with 95% of its space already leased despite premium prices. The tower's central location and state-of-the-art facilities make it a highly desirable hub for the tech industry, though early tenants are currently contending with construction noise and dust.

title: Angie's List is selling its 25-building East Washington Street campus and moving out
summary: ANGI Homeservices Inc. is putting Angie's List's sprawling east-side campus up for sale and relocating up to 1,000 employees to other offices in Indianapolis. The property, consisting of 25 buildings and 190,000 square feet, is being listed by JLL, with a buyer expected to be identified within a few weeks and employees relocated by mid-2018. This move follows months of speculation after HomeAdvisor parent company IAC acquired Angie's List, and local stakeholders are keen for the new buyer to engage with the surrounding community.

title: How Clorox grew its e-commerce business 50 percent
summary: The Clorox Company increased its e-commerce business by 50 percent overall and 98 percent on Amazon alone by focusing on digital marketing, including paid search on Amazon and leveraging its in-house data management platform. E-commerce now represents 4 percent of Clorox's total sales, and the company views Amazon as both a merchandising and marketing channel. Clorox uses lookalike audience targeting and sponsored ads on Amazon to drive sales and brand awareness, while also focusing on storytelling for branding.

title: Walmart (WMT) Stock Soars on Guidance, $20 Billion Buyback
summary: Walmart (WMT) stock rose over 4% after the company announced strong fiscal 2019 guidance, including 3% sales growth and 40% online sales growth, alongside a new $20 billion stock buyback program. This strategic focus on online sales and grocery initiatives is seen as a direct effort to compete with Amazon and is paying off, with Walmart projected to achieve 5% EPS growth in 2019. Despite a tough retail environment, WMT's stock is up more than 20% year-to-date.

title: Now Open: Lemonade Shares API Platform With ‘The World’
summary: Lemonade announced the launch of a public API allowing developers to integrate insurance offerings into their own apps and websites. This initiative aims to make insurance more accessible and hassle-free, allowing partners to offer instant coverage for renters, condo, and homeowners insurance in Lemonade's active markets. The company likens this move to "liberating technology" adopted by companies like Amazon and Apple, enabling a broader ecosystem for insurance services.

title: Kroger Weighs Sale of Convenience Stores
summary: Kroger Co. is considering selling its nearly 800 convenience stores and implementing other cost-cutting measures to compete with new rivals like Amazon.com Inc. Executives believe the convenience stores, which primarily sell gas, could generate higher returns through a sale than their current profitability within the company. This move is part of the nation's largest traditional grocer's strategy to invest in e-commerce and adapt to the changing retail landscape.

title: Western Digital Aims Largest Hard Drive Ever at World’s Largest Data Centers
summary: Western Digital has developed the world's first 14TB hard drive, the HGST Ultrastar Hs14, specifically targeting hyper-scale cloud operators like Facebook, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Tencent, and Alibaba. This new drive utilizes shingled magnetic recording (SMR) and fourth-generation HelioSeal technology to offer increased storage capacity and reduced power consumption, making it ideal for backup and archiving in large data centers. While Western Digital leads in introducing such high-capacity drives, competitors like Seagate Technology LLC and Toshiba Corp. are expected to follow suit.

title: Amazon said to test delivery service to rival FedEx, UPS
summary: Amazon is reportedly testing a new delivery service called "Seller Flex" in the U.S., aiming to expand eligibility for free two-day delivery and relieve warehouse congestion. This initiative would deepen Amazon's involvement in delivery functions typically handled by UPS and FedEx, giving Amazon more control over the last mile to customers and potentially reducing costs. The move could pressure the shares of traditional carriers as Amazon expands further into logistics.

title: The Week in Review: IoT
summary: This article reviews the Internet of Things (IoT) market, highlighting significant growth forecasts, major investments by companies like Dell Technologies and Alibaba, and new product developments. It details market projections by IDC, various company initiatives in IoT, recent funding rounds for cybersecurity startups in the IoT space, and partnerships aimed at advancing IoT solutions.

title: Pfizer looks to relocate office to E. Memphis in $19.6M investment
summary: Pfizer is planning a $19.6 million investment to relocate its Memphis offices to a new development in East Memphis. The pharmaceutical company will join Strategic Financial Partners and Pinnacle Financial Partners as tenants in Boyle's new building. This move signifies a significant investment by Pfizer in the East Memphis area.

title: Amazon bets on Atlanta tech with office expansions
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is significantly expanding its tech presence in Atlanta, which currently employs 300 tech workers. This expansion positions Atlanta as one of Amazon's key regional tech hubs across the country, indicating a growing investment in the city's technology sector.

title: Ahold Delhaize CEO focused on integration amid talk of Kroger deal
summary: Ahold Delhaize CEO Dick Boer downplayed the possibility of acquiring Kroger, emphasizing the company's current focus on integrating its own 2016 merger. Despite speculation, Boer highlighted the need to deliver synergies from the existing deal, while still acknowledging that the company always keeps an eye on market developments. He also defended the enduring role of brick-and-mortar grocery stores against the rise of online alternatives.

title: Las Vegas ballpark design revealed for master-planned desert community
summary: The Howard Hughes Corporation unveiled the preliminary design for the new 10,000-capacity Las Vegas Ballpark in Summerlin, designed by HOK, to house the Triple-A baseball team, the 51s. This ballpark is part of a larger 400-acre "Downtown Summerlin" development, aiming to create a more urban environment with offices, parks, and residential units. The design draws inspiration from the desert landscape and Howard Hughes' aviation legacy, with construction expected to start early next year and open for the 2019 season.

title: Sonos One review: Sweet sound mixed with Alexa voice and smart home controls
summary: The Sonos One is reviewed as a smart speaker offering excellent sound quality and integrated Alexa voice controls without needing an Amazon Echo. While it functions well as a smart home assistant and music player for numerous services, it lacks some Alexa features like Drop In and voice calling due to not being an Amazon device. The speaker is also slated to receive Google Assistant integration in 2018, expanding its voice assistant compatibility.

title: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings Joins Forbes List of Richest Americans
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings has joined the Forbes 400 list of richest Americans for the first time with a net worth of $2.3 billion, largely due to the surge in Netflix's stock. He debuted at number 359 on the list, which required a minimum net worth of $2 billion this year. The article also touches on Netflix's strong Q3 subscriber growth and content spending projections, and lists other notable billionaires on the Forbes 400.

title: These Cheap Impact Wrenches Will Give Your Toolbox Some Serious Power
summary: This article highlights several Ingersoll Rand tools available at discounted prices on Amazon for one day only. Featured items include the Quiet Titanium Air Impact Wrench, the Short Barrel Air Hammer Kit, and a 1/2-Inch High-Torque Impactool Kit, detailing their features and cost savings. These tools are presented as powerful options for automotive and industrial projects.

title: Amazon beat out F5 Networks for Rainier Square tower
summary: Amazon secured a major office lease in the 58-story Rainier Square tower, outbidding F5 Networks for the space. This deal highlights the intense competition among companies for prime workplace environments and locations in Seattle.

title: Target is ramping up delivery, and opening new stores
summary: Target is expanding its same-day delivery services and utilizing 1,400 stores for online order fulfillment during the holiday season. The company is also opening new smaller-format stores in urban areas and college campuses, aiming to open 130 by 2019, while also remodeling existing locations to boost sales. These initiatives are part of Target's strategy to compete with other retailers in fast delivery and expand its market share.

title: Amazon Prime is popular, but in three-quarters of all U.S homes? That's open to debate
summary: The article discusses the varying estimates of Amazon Prime membership in the U.S., with figures ranging from less than half to three-quarters of all households. While Amazon doesn't release official numbers, different research firms and analysts offer conflicting data and perspectives on Prime's true market penetration and its impact on Amazon's market power and the retail landscape. The popularity of Prime is acknowledged, but its overall dominance compared to traditional retailers like Walmart is debated.

title: Meet Bill Boeing, the granddaddy of Seattle’s tech scene
summary: This article traces the surprising influence of William E. Boeing, founder of The Boeing Company, on Seattle's modern tech landscape. It highlights how Boeing, an entrepreneur from the early 20th century, shared characteristics with today's tech innovators like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk, transforming Seattle into an economic powerhouse. The piece argues that Boeing's entrepreneurial spirit and vision laid the groundwork for the city's current tech success despite the company's eventual departure.

title: HPE to Stop Selling Commodity Servers to Hyper-Scale Cloud Companies
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is exiting the business of selling commodity servers to hyper-scale cloud providers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Alibaba. The company will instead focus on selling higher-margin hardware, such as high-end servers and hyper-converged infrastructure, to traditional enterprises and some tier-1 cloud players. This strategic shift is a response to the tough competition and low margins in the commodity server market, especially as cloud giants increasingly design their own hardware.

title: Why DryShips, PetMed Express, and VF Corp. Jumped Today
summary: Despite a down day for the broader stock market, DryShips, PetMed Express, and VF Corp. saw significant gains. DryShips benefited from a rise in the Baltic Dry Index, PetMed Express reported strong fiscal second-quarter results with increased sales and net income, and VF Corp. saw revenue growth from brands like Vans and boosted its full-year outlook and dividend.

title: Sears to stop selling Benton Harbor-based Whirlpool appliances after 100 years
authors: ['Tribune Staff and Wire Report', 'Caleb Bauer', 'The Associated Press']
summary: Sears will cease selling Whirlpool appliances, ending a century-long business relationship. Whirlpool stated the decision was made in May due to an inability to agree on terms for Whirlpool-branded products, though it will continue to supply Kenmore products to Sears. This split highlights Sears' ongoing struggles against competitors like Home Depot and Amazon.

title: AIEQ Chart | Amplify AI Powered Equity ETF
summary: This page provides a live, interactive chart for the Amplify AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ) on NYSE, allowing users to analyze historical data and apply various technical indicators. The chart is highly customizable, offering different chart types and a range of technical tools for detailed market analysis. It also displays real-time market data for major indices, commodities, and individual stocks.

title: Whole Foods, Amazon style: Store near Union Station will serve alcohol, sell electronics (Photos)
summary: Whole Foods is opening a 50,000-square-foot flagship store near Denver's Union Station on November 15th. This new location, described as "Amazon style," will not only sell traditional groceries but also serve alcohol and sell electronics, marking a new approach for the natural-foods chain. The store is situated on the ground floor of the Union Denver complex.

title: Sears-Whirlpool curtail relationship after 100 years
summary: Sears announced it will no longer sell Whirlpool-branded appliances, ending a century-long business relationship. This decision stems from demands by Whirlpool that Sears claimed would make selling their products uncompetitive. The move highlights Sears' ongoing struggles against online retailers and big-box stores, as both companies saw their stock prices fall following the announcement.

title: Cisco and Google Find Mutual Interest in Cloud Computing (Published 2017)
summary: Google and Cisco Systems are partnering to help companies manage software and technology services across their own data centers and external cloud platforms. This collaboration allows Google to leverage Cisco's corporate ties to compete with Amazon in cloud services, while Cisco seeks to counter the threat cloud services pose to its traditional hardware business. Both companies, once dominant in different internet eras, are adapting to the evolving landscape of cloud computing.

title: Kroger names new COO, consolidates power among top chiefs
summary: Kroger has appointed Mike Donnelly, formerly executive vice president of merchandising, as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective November 1. This move is part of the company's "Restock Kroger Plan" and centralizes power among its experienced executive team. Concurrently, Fred Morganthall, executive vice president of retail operations, will retire after 44 years in the industry.

title: WW Grainger shares drop after Amazon launches Business Prime Shipping
summary: W.W. Grainger shares dropped over 3 percent after Amazon Business launched its Business Prime Shipping service, offering free two-day shipping to multi-user business accounts. Analysts believe Grainger will face increased price competition due to Amazon's "deep pockets and apparent margin insensitivity." The new service directly competes with Grainger's Japanese and British operations, which combined account for 11 percent of its total sales.

title: ANSYS Startup Program Gives Affordable CAE, HPC and Cloud to the Masses
summary: ANSYS and Rescale have partnered to launch a startup program that offers affordable access to CAE, HPC, and cloud resources to small businesses. This initiative aims to remove the financial barriers preventing startups from utilizing advanced simulation tools, leveraging Amazon Web Services for cloud storage and compute power. The program's cost varies based on the startup's maturity and needs, making high-quality engineering simulation accessible without significant upfront hardware investments.

title: Cool Factor And Name Brands Distinguish Two Rivers Coffee In Single-Cup Space
summary: Two Rivers Coffee has become a major player in the single-cup coffee market by differentiating itself with trendy, fun brands, innovative packaging, and licensing iconic national brands like Tootsie Roll and Junior Mints. The company, founded by Mayer Koenig and Eugene and Steven Schreiber, expanded from retail into office coffee service, where its modern product line appeals to younger workplace consumers. Two Rivers continues to focus on innovation, creating its own unique brands and varieties while also partnering with big-name brands for flavored coffees and hot chocolates, ensuring continued growth and market presence.

title: How Much Do People Want to Pay for Netflix? Less Than It’s Charging for Standard Plan
summary: A Morning Consult survey indicates that 91% of U.S. adults would pay up to $10 per month for Netflix, which is less than the new standard plan price of $10.99. Despite this, Netflix maintains an 80% favorability rating, and many subscribers are not deterred by the recent $1 price increase. The article suggests that Netflix's ability to offer original content will continue to justify its price to customers.

title: Wal-Mart's new robots scan shelves to restock items faster
summary: Wal-Mart is deploying shelf-scanning robots in over 50 U.S. stores to accelerate inventory replenishment and free up employee time. These 2-foot robots use cameras to identify out-of-stock, misplaced, or mislabeled items, relaying data to staff for corrections. The initiative aims to improve sales lost due to unavailable products and is part of Wal-Mart's broader strategy to digitize stores and enhance shopping efficiency.

title: Pat Stryker and President Trump Tie on List of Richest Billionaires
summary: Fort Collins resident Pat Stryker and President Donald Trump are tied for No. 248 on Forbes' list of America’s richest billionaires, each with an estimated net worth of $3.1 billion. They share this spot with 14 other individuals. The article also lists the top five wealthiest billionaires, with Bill Gates at number one.

title: Payne: First Tesla Michigan gallery opens at Somerset mall
summary: Tesla Inc. has opened its first stand-alone gallery space in Michigan at the Somerset Collection mall in Troy. This gallery, similar to an Apple store and located next to one, allows customers to learn about Tesla vehicles and energy products but not purchase cars directly due to Michigan's direct-to-consumer sales ban. The opening comes as Tesla battles state laws restricting its direct sales model, showcasing Model S and Model X vehicles, and highlighting its maintenance approach for electric vehicles.

title: Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Intel find billions more in profit
summary: Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Intel significantly exceeded profit and revenue expectations in their third-quarter earnings reports. Collectively, these four tech giants increased their profits by approximately $2.2 billion and revenue by $19 billion compared to the previous year. Their stock prices rose in after-hours trading, further boosting their combined market capitalization.

title: Buck's Sporting Goods to shutter retail operation
summary: After nearly nine decades, Buck's Sporting Goods is closing its retail operation in Amarillo due to declining sales from internet competition and larger retailers. Owner Gary Hillers is selling the retail location to Athletic Supply Inc., but the company will continue to operate its more profitable school division from the current location, servicing over 40 school districts. The retail store will officially close its doors on December 31, 2017, marking the end of its public storefront presence.
